title: NY State Assembly · District 26
area: Northeast Queens, including Bayside, Douglaston, Little Neck, Auburndale and parts of Flushing and Whitestone.

context.text: Incumbent Edward Braunstein advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot. Robert Speranza defeated Philip Grillo 61.5%-37.8% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary to again face Braunstein, whom he also ran against in 2022 and 2024.

summary.text: Edward Braunstein is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 26 in Northeast Queens. He was born and raised in Bayside, worked as a legislative assistant in the Assembly Speaker's New York City office, and was first elected to the Assembly in 2010. He chairs the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee and is seeking re-election in 2026.

background.text: Born and raised in Bayside, Queens; according to his official Assembly biography, he lives in Bay Terrace with his wife, Stephanie, and their three children.
Earned a B.S. in Finance from the State University of New York at Albany in 2003 and a J.D. from New York Law School in 2008; his Assembly biography says he passed the bar exam in February 2009.

Before his election, worked as a legislative assistant in the Assembly Speaker's New York City office (Ballotpedia names the Speaker as Sheldon Silver) and served on Community Board 11, which covers Northeast Queens neighborhoods.
Elected to the New York State Assembly in 2010 to represent the 26th District in Northeast Queens, and took office in 2011.

Chairs the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee (2025-2026) and serves on the Health, Judiciary, Rules and Ways and Means committees; chaired the Cities Committee from 2019 through 2024.
His Assembly biography says his first bill to be signed into law, banning so-called "bath salts," was enacted in July 2011 (Chapter 130 of 2011).

According to the same biography, he also sponsored laws making the unlicensed practice of law a felony (Chapter 492 of 2012), requiring campuses to notify local law enforcement of on-campus violent crimes and missing persons (Chapter 486 of 2014), and establishing the crime of unlawful dissemination or publication of an intimate image (Chapter 109 of 2019).

positions.summary: Sponsored A02047, creating a real-property tax abatement and exemption for capital improvements that reduce carbon emissions, with co-sponsors including David Weprin and Nily Rozic.

record.text: Chairs the Assembly Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee (2025-2026), which has jurisdiction over the Public Service Commission and utility regulation; also serves on the Health, Judiciary, Rules, and Ways and Means committees. Previously chaired the Cities Committee (2021-2024).

Sponsored A08675 ("prevention of damage to critical infrastructure act"), restricting junk and scrap dealers from buying metals used by critical infrastructure providers; passed the Assembly on March 9, 2026, amended and repassed May 18, 2026, and was substituted into Senate companion bill S8302-D, which passed the Senate on June 4, 2026 and was returned to the Assembly.

Sponsored A10422, requiring that any Public Service Commission sanction or civil penalty against a utility be returned to ratepayers as a direct bill credit within 90 days; the Assembly bill was substituted by Senate companion bill S8908, which passed the Assembly on June 4, 2026.

Sponsored A02429, directing the Department of Public Service to report on the affordability of water services for residential and commercial customers; referred to the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.
Sponsored A02047, establishing a property-tax abatement and exemption for capital improvements that reduce carbon emissions; referred to committee, not enacted as of this writing.

candidates.name: Robert Speranza

summary.text: Robert Speranza is the Republican nominee for NY State Assembly District 26, defeating Philip Grillo in the June 2026 Republican primary. According to his campaign website, he is a retired NYPD officer and lifelong Bayside resident who began his career as a NYC probation officer. He previously ran against incumbent Edward Braunstein in the 2022 and 2024 general elections, losing both.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a lifelong resident of Bayside who attended Holy Cross High School and graduated from St. John's University with a B.S. in Criminal Justice.
According to his campaign website, he began his career as a NYC Probation Officer and then joined the NYPD, where he says he served for 20 years; he describes himself as a retired NYPD officer.

His campaign website lists earlier volunteer and civic roles including the NYPD Auxiliary Police, the Bayside Ambulance Corps, Queens Community Board 11, an executive board seat at a local hospital, and the Fraternal Order of Police and Knights of Columbus as an officer.

Ran against Edward Braunstein in the 2022 general election, receiving 45.5% of the vote on the Republican and Conservative lines, and again in 2024 on the Conservative and Common Sense lines, receiving 31.9%; Braunstein won both.
Won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary over Philip Grillo, 61.5% to 37.8%, to become the Republican nominee.
